decisions.reason: After two years this manual laser workstation line still fits the firm's laser portfolio and is worth keeping as a niche option, but its less digital and more manual positioning plus overlap with newer laser cabins raise its withdrawal risk.

This thermal inkjet printer is very close to the firm's core applications and customer base, so in a growing market a large R&D-active firm would typically keep it on the market while building sales and service experience.
As a flagship 2024 launch shown on the home page and aligned with the firm's Industry 4.0 direction, these industrial laser systems are very unlikely to be abandoned so soon.

The compact laser marking cabin is a recent, strategically related launch, so real-options logic favors keeping it while demand becomes clearer, although some portfolio overlap with other enclosed laser solutions remains.

The lubricant printing system for sheet metal has positive early validation from its trade-fair award and extends the firm's coding know-how into a promising niche, so it is likely to be retained despite some application-specific uncertainty.
